attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (/root/wireguard-gateway/site.yml, run from node4 the control_node) that serves a demo application on node2:8080, and restricts node3 to reach it only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1. node1 (VyOS) hosts the in-kernel WireGuard endpoint; node3 (RHEL7, no in-kernel WG module available on this old kernel) uses a userspace wireguard-go binary built from source with a self-installed Go 1.23 toolchain, wired into wg-quick's documented kernel-module fallback. node1 hairpin-NATs tunneled traffic to its own LAN IP before it reaches node2, and node2's firewalld only accepts port 8080 from node1's LAN address, so any direct node3->node2 attempt is dropped while the tunneled path succeeds (confirmed node2's access log shows node1 as the source). Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes, capturing changed boot_id plus recovered services/tunnel/app on each. Along the way diagnosed and fixed a kernel WireGuard peer-state wedge on node1 that appeared after a redundant config re-apply, by deleting and recreating the wg0 interface, after which handshakes and application access were reconfirmed working.
